A windswept mountain crag high above the clouds, jagged grey rock falling away into a sea of mist, distant snowy peaks catching the cold light.
A storm-tossed open sea under a black sky, mountainous waves heaving, rain slashing sideways, a doomed ship tiny in the distance.
An ancient deep forest of colossal moss-furred trunks, green light filtering through the high canopy, ferns and mist on the floor fading into gloom.
A volcanic wasteland of cracked black basalt, rivers of molten rock casting hellish orange light upward, ash drifting like grey snow through choking air.
A misty moor at dusk, pale sedge grass stretching endlessly, dark pools reflecting nothing, a low fog swallowing distance and horizon alike.
A ruined temple overgrown by centuries of jungle, carved stone faces half-buried in roots, shafts of dusty light piercing the canopy onto crumbled altars.
A frozen tundra under a vast colourless sky, permafrost cracking in geometric patterns, a bitter wind driving ice crystals low across the featureless white plain.
A sun-baked desert canyon of blood-red sandstone, sheer walls pressing close, the sky a pale hot sliver above, shadows pooling deep in the dry riverbed below.
A deep sea-cave barely lit by bioluminescent growth, black water filling the chamber floor, stalactites dripping into absolute silence far from any surface light.
A labyrinthine cavern of towering limestone columns, underground rivers murmuring in unseen passages, the darkness layered and complete beyond the faint glow of mineral veins.
A blighted swamp of dead cypress standing in black water, phosphorescent fungi clinging to rotted bark, thick fog diffusing the weak light into a sickly yellow smear.
A cliff over a churning ocean, raw white water exploding against the rocks far below, salt spray rising in curtains, grey sky merging with the sea at the edge of sight.
A moonlit glade ringed by silver birch, the full moon hanging low and enormous, blue-white light pooling on the dew-soaked grass and vanishing at the treeline.
A battlefield of old bones stretching to a flat horizon, rusted armour half-submerged in mud, crows circling above, the sky the colour of a weeks-old bruise.
A glacial valley carved smooth by ancient ice, blue-green walls of compacted snow rising on either side, meltwater trickling over polished stone in near-total silence.
A sunken city beneath shallow tropical water, coral colonising the pale stone towers, filtered sunlight playing in shifting patterns over streets now navigated by fish.
A high alpine meadow above the treeline, short bright wildflowers trembling in thin cold wind, the land falling sharply away on three sides into a blue void of distance.
A tar pit plain under a leaden sky, dark viscous pools bubbling slowly, bones of enormous creatures half-emerged and tilting at strange angles, the air reeking of pitch.
A salt flat under brutal midday sun, the white crust blinding and boundless, heat shimmer erasing the horizon, no shadow anywhere for miles in any direction.
A subterranean fungal forest, enormous pale caps arching overhead, spores drifting like slow snow through still air, faint violet light emanating from the mycelium threading the ground.
A sea-stack archipelago lashed by permanent storm, narrow columns of rock rising from white water, seabirds screaming in the updraft, the mainland lost somewhere beyond dark rain.
A petrified woodland of stone trees still standing, grey trunks frozen mid-growth for aeons, silence absolute, the ground carpeted in mineral dust, pale sky visible through rigid stone branches.
A river delta at flood season, brown water spreading across flat land in every direction, half-drowned palms marking old channels, the sky enormous and storm-lit at the edge.
A cinder field beneath a smoking caldera, black gravel crunching underfoot for miles, heat rising in visible waves, the cone above glowing dull red against a starless night.
A flooded cathedral ruin, vaulted arches still standing knee-deep in dark water, stained-glass fragments refracting pale light across submerged flagstones, silence broken only by distant dripping.
